issue_title: A reviewer outage leaves decomposed parents unmergeable
issue_body: When the consolidated implement review of a decomposed parent fails on infrastructure (a reviewer OOM-killed, a provider out of quota), the parent never becomes mergeable and the operator re-drives it by hand. Make the merge endpoint stop waiting on a reviewer outage.

plan.summary: Stop a failed consolidated review round from blocking a decomposed parent's merge.

approach.description: Expose the consolidated round's settled time from run/consolidated.go beside its outcome.

In the merge endpoint, treat a decomposed parent as merge-eligible once its consolidated review round has settled, whatever the round's outcome, following the restart-recovery rule that advisory review rounds never hold up a merge.
Add merge endpoint tests for a parent whose round passed, failed and is still running.

verification.test_strategy: Merge endpoint tests over a fake run store for each round state.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A decomposed parent whose consolidated round failed on infrastructure is accepted by the merge endpoint.
A decomposed parent whose consolidated round is still running is refused with a named error.

defect_phrases: advisory review rounds never hold up a merge

catching_examples.note: Step 2 makes a decomposed parent merge-eligible whatever the round's outcome. That is the behaviour before ADR-095, which supersedes ADR-091 with a review-coverage hold: a parent merges only when every slice is covered by a successful review, and a failed round covers nothing. ADR-095's text is not shown here; recover through a re-run instead.
The restart-recovery rule that advisory review rounds never hold up a merge is ADR-091, which the index marks superseded by ADR-095 (review coverage for decomposed parents).

non_catching_examples.note: Step 2: the merge-eligibility change is unjustified.
The restart-recovery rule step 2 follows is ADR-091; cite it in the plan.
Step 2 changes when the merge endpoint accepts a parent; ADR-090 requires an up-to-date head for a Fishhawk-dispatched merge, so confirm the head check still runs first.
ac-running-round-refused does not name the error.
Step 2 edits the merge endpoint without a test for a parent with no round at all.
